note: Existing-source, strict-license-screened public gallery. Additional historical photos remain held from this site. Anatomy overlays are teaching annotations, not a separate verified voucher determination.

tiles.heading: 01 · INTERRUPTED NARROW PERENNIAL HEAD
tiles.details: Reverchon's bristlegrass is a perennial with short, sometimes knotty rhizomes; culms roughly 30–90 cm. Panicles ~5–20 cm may look interrupted, unlike the longer loose bottlebrush of S. scheelei. Archived image indices 0–2 support gross head shape but cannot verify a rooted rhizome or bristle insertion.
tiles.short: LOOK HERE FIRST: narrow upright flowering axis with visibly separated spikelet groups
tiles.status: FIELD PHOTO — SAME-PLANT RHIZOME AND HEAD NEEDED

tiles.heading: 02 · TRUE STIFF-HAIR LIGULE
tiles.details: Do not mistake longer collar or sheath hairs for the ligule. Blade width roughly 1–7 mm, varying with position. No current image clearly isolates the actual 1–2 mm hair fringe with a scale; a source-labelled leaf without a visible junction is not ligule proof.
tiles.short: At the blade–sheath junction find a ~1–2 mm fringe of stiff hairs

tiles.heading: 03 · SPARSE PERSISTENT BRISTLES
tiles.details: The regional UT treatment reports shorter curved bristles to ~2 mm; FNA documents ~2–8 mm. Do not impose a universal ≤2 mm rule. These are persistent sterile branchlets, NOT lemma awns. Existing panicle overview does not resolve insertion or allow counting. Sample multiple ripe attachments under 10–20×.
tiles.short: At each attached spikelet base, bristles may be absent or sparse, ~2–8 mm where present (FNA)

tiles.heading: 04 · MATURE SPIKELET ~2.1–4.5 MM
tiles.details: The lower glume is about HALF spikelet length, usually 5–7-veined; upper glume nearly reaches the fertile lemma, usually 7–9-veined. These proportional characters are from botanical treatments, not existing photos. Avoid inventing exact millimeters for separate glumes without a specimen.
tiles.short: Measure several ripe elliptical spikelets with a 1-mm bar; UT local ~3–3.6 mm
tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — SEPARATED GLUMES AND CALIBRATED SPIKELET

tiles.heading: 05 · WRINKLED FERTILE LEMMA, NO LONG AWN
tiles.details: The upper fertile lemma and palea are firm; the lower sterile palea is absent in the cited FNA description. No projecting long true glume/lemma awn; visible bristles belong to sterile branchlets. Photograph a mature dissected ~2.1–4.5 mm spikelet and true transverse rugosity before annotating.
tiles.short: Lower sterile lemma near fertile lemma length; hard upper fertile lemma finely cross-wrinkled

tiles.heading: 06 · COMPARE THREE LOCAL FOXTAILS
tiles.details: S. parviflora commonly has 4–12 bristles per spikelet and a shorter denser head; S. scheelei usually one conspicuous 10–35 mm bristle with a tapering head; S. italica is a fibrous-rooted annual with heavy dense head. Counts and head silhouettes overlap in poor photos: check mature spikelet base, true ligule and rooted perennial habit.
tiles.short: Sparse interrupted head versus S. parviflora's many bristles and S. scheelei's long mostly solitary bristles
tiles.status: FIELD COMPARISON — MATCHED BRISTLE BASES PENDING

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: REVERCHON'S BRISTLEGRASS (perennial): the existing real photo shows a skinny, often interrupted upright flowering head, with widely separated spikelet groupings. Its bristles are sparse—some spikelets appear almost unbristled—but FNA gives bristles about 2–8 mm where present; do NOT teach a hard ≤2 mm cutoff. Seek short knotty rhizomes, the stiff hair ligule (1–2 mm), and mature 2.1–4.5 mm spikelets. No bristle measurement is visible in the original picture.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: START with the local Eric Knight interrupted-head overview (panel 1). Two Patrick Alexander CC0 photographs have now been JPEG/pixel inspected: panel 2 shows distinctly spaced real spikelets along the axis; panel 3 shows narrow leaf and hairs at its junction. Four new arrows point only to those gross photographed structures.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Do not mistake longer collar or sheath hairs for the ligule. Blade width roughly 1–7 mm, varying with position. No current image clearly isolates the actual 1–2 mm hair fringe with a scale; a source-labelled leaf without a visible junction is not ligule proof.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: The lower glume is about HALF spikelet length, usually 5–7-veined; upper glume nearly reaches the fertile lemma, usually 7–9-veined. These proportional characters are from botanical treatments, not existing photos. Avoid inventing exact millimeters for separate glumes without a specimen.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

steps.title: 5 · Compare similar grasses
steps.look_for: Compared with S. parviflora, Reverchon's bristlegrass has a more interrupted narrow head and much fewer attached bristles (parviflora typically 4–12 per spikelet). S. scheelei has conspicuously long spreading bristles commonly 10–35 mm and a longer tapering head, often broad hairy leaves. Millet S. italica is an annual crop/escape with heavy dense terminal heads. Panicle texture varies with maturity, so verify bristles at the spikelet base.
steps.why_it_matters: Confirm at least two independent botanical characters; do not remove a native candidate from color alone.

panels.label: DUVAL COUNTY · one living tuft with narrow blades and attached green flowering heads
panels.caption: Clifton Ladd photographed Setaria reverchonii in Duval County, Texas. The living tuft has several narrow blades emerging low on the shoots and at least three upright, interrupted green flowering heads. The hand holds basal culms together; it does NOT expose actual nodal rhizomes, fibrous roots or inner ligule. This same observation supplies the next closer photo.

intro: REVERCHON'S BRISTLEGRASS (perennial): the existing real photo shows a skinny, often interrupted upright flowering head, with widely separated spikelet groupings. Its bristles are sparse—some spikelets appear almost unbristled—but FNA gives bristles about 2–8 mm where present; do NOT teach a hard ≤2 mm cutoff. Seek short knotty rhizomes, the stiff hair ligule (1–2 mm), and mature 2.1–4.5 mm spikelets. No bristle measurement is visible in the original picture.
memory_rule: MILLET=ANNUAL HEAVY HEAD (usually 1–3 bristles); PARVIFLORA=KNOTTY RHIZOME + MANY (4–12); REVERCHONII=INTERRUPTED SPARSE (2–8 mm where bristled); SCHEELEI=LONG SINGLE (10–35 mm).
safety_note: Three exact-species JPEGs already physically archived, all three featured; existing first-panel gross arrows preserved. UT local bristle description (to ~2 mm) and FNA broader range (2–8 mm) differ by source/scope. No photo in this gallery resolves the bristle base, ligule or glume nerves with a calibrated scale. No new JPEG or fine arrow asserted. 2026-10-26: CC BY-NC S. scheelei comparative panel swapped for verified-in-repository CC0 S. scheelei whole-plant comparison; three inherited original-pixel gross arrows, not new bristle-level evidence. Two Patrick Alexander archived JPEGs were independently pixel-inspected at source 3600×2400 October 26, and found clean of EXIF, with four gross anatomy arrows. Spikelet attachment positions and sheath-region hairs are shown, NOT bristle origin, separate glume nerves, mm dimensions or the authentic true ligule.
field_rule: Sparse interrupted flowering axis + fewer bristles, sometimes absent at terminal upper spikelets; verify BRISTLE INSERTION on branchlet and perennial knotty base, not a guessed hair arrow.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
comparison_text: Compared with S. parviflora, Reverchon's bristlegrass has a more interrupted narrow head and much fewer attached bristles (parviflora typically 4–12 per spikelet). S. scheelei has conspicuously long spreading bristles commonly 10–35 mm and a longer tapering head, often broad hairy leaves. Millet S. italica is an annual crop/escape with heavy dense terminal heads. Panicle texture varies with maturity, so verify bristles at the spikelet base.
